_description: Architectural decision records: routing, state management, build pipeline, major library choices, cross-cutting refactors. Append only; supersede with a new entry instead of editing.

title: Three-layer split: app / server / shared (types only)
context: Need clear separation of concerns and a single secure home for AI keys. Alternatives considered: monorepo packages; Nuxt 3 pattern with no explicit shared layer.
decision: Three-layer split: app (client), server, shared (types only). Layer boundaries enforced at the import level; Nuxt 4 auto-imports shared types on both sides.
rationale: Security: AI keys never leave the server. Testability: server logic is pure Node with no DOM dependency. Clarity: each layer has one responsibility and a clear import direction.
consequences_positive: Layer boundaries are enforced at the import level; Nuxt 4 auto-imports shared types on both sides

title: Shared types via Nuxt 4 auto-imports from shared/types/
context: Need a single source of truth for the client-server API contract without manual import boilerplate. Alternatives considered: separate npm package for shared types; manual imports in each file.
decision: Shared types live in shared/types/ and are auto-imported on both client and server by Nuxt 4.
rationale: Single source of truth for the client-server API contract. No manual import statements. Shape errors are caught at compile time on both sides simultaneously.
consequences_positive: Types are always in sync; no import boilerplate

title: Game data as TS consts in server/data/, never sent raw to client
context: Rulebook text is copyright-protected and must stay server-private. Alternatives considered: database; client-accessible JSON files.
decision: Game data is stored as TypeScript constants under server/data/ and is never shipped raw to the client.
rationale: Copyright: rulebook text stays server-private. Type safety: shape errors caught at compile time. No DB needed for initial versions.
consequences_positive: Data is typed, server-private, and zero-dependency; DB migration would only touch server/services/rpg/
